title: Coefficient-field orthogonality in a Gauss spectral extension
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value, and stable [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field]. Fix $n\ge1$, put $R=k(X_1,\ldots,X_n)=\operatorname{Frac}(k[X_1,\ldots,X_n])$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and give $R$ the Gauss absolute value $|f/g|=\max_
u|f_
u|/\max_
u|g_
u|$. For every finite field extension $E/R$ let $s=s_{E/R}$ be the minimal-polynomial spectral norm [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm]. Every finite-dimensional $k$-linear subspace $V\subset E$ has a $k$-basis $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ with $s(\sum_i a_iv_i)=\max_i|a_i|s(v_i)$ for all $a_i\in k$. For $V=0$ the basis is empty and the maximum is $0$. The dimension here is over $k$, not over $R$; no assertion that $E$ has an orthogonal $R$-basis is included.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.3/2, printed pp.214–215 (scan PDF pp.220–221). Primary scan read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $T=k\langle X\rangle$, $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(T)$, and $H=\widehat R$. By [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] polynomial truncations are Gauss-dense in $T$; by [lem-trf-tate-gauss-multiplicative] the Gauss norm is multiplicative. Consequently $Q$ embeds isometrically into $H$: approximate numerator and nonzero denominator by polynomials. An approximation $g_j\to g\ne0$ has $G(g_j)=G(g)$ eventually, and $|g_j^{-1}-g_l^{-1}|=G(g_j-g_l)/(G(g_j)G(g_l))\to0$, so these fractions define the embedding. Apply [lem-trf-spectral-completion-scalar-envelope] with $F=R$ to form $E\subset M\subset\mathcal C$. Write $\sigma=\sigma_{M/Q}$. Its statement gives $\sigma|_E=s$ and $N(qz)=|q|_QN(z)$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.3/2, p.215: diagram and comparison of spectral norms.

proof.text: Choose an $R$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_m$ of $E$. For each $e_i$ choose its monic minimal relation $e_i^{r_i}+\sum_j c_{ij}e_i^{r_i-j}=0$, and a nonzero polynomial $h_i\in k[X]$ clearing all $c_{ij}$ denominators. Then $l_i=h_ie_i$ satisfies the monic relation with coefficients $h_i^jc_{ij}\in k[X]$. Thus $l_i$ is integral over $T$. Put $A=T[l_1,\ldots,l_m]\subset M$. Reducing powers by these monic relations shows that the finitely many monomials $\prod_i l_i^{b_i}$ with $0\le b_i<r_i$ span $A$ over $T$. It is reduced since $M$ is, and torsion-free since nonzero elements of $T$ are units in $Q$. Its localization by $T\setminus\{0\}$ equals $Q[l_1,\ldots,l_m]=M$: the $l_i$ span $E$ over $R$, and products of elements of $E$ stay in $E$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.3/2, p.215: choose integral generators and form the finite Tate model.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-tate-finite-algebra-norming-evaluations] for this $T\hookrightarrow A$. Every $0\ne a\in A$ has a $k$-linear evaluation $\chi_a:A\to k_a$ contractive for $\sigma$ and attaining $\sigma(a)$. The restricted function $\sigma|_A$ is a definite ultrametric $k$-vector norm: for each $a$ its evaluation attains its value, hence $\sigma(a)=\sup_\chi s_{k_\chi/k}(\chi(a))$ over these contractive maps; the norm axioms follow from those of [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm] in each target, and definiteness also follows from the strict positivity asserted by the evaluation lemma. Since $k$ is stable, [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field] gives an orthogonal $k$-basis of each finite $k_a$. Therefore [lem-trf-norming-maps-cartesian-criterion] applies to $(A,\sigma)$: every finite $k$-subspace of $A$ is orthogonally based.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.3/2, p.215: application of Proposition 3.8.1/11, expanded using 3.8.1/7 and 3.8.1/10.

proof.text: Let $V\subset E$ have finite $k$-basis $v_1,\ldots,v_d$. Each $v_i$ is an $R$-linear combination of the $l_j$, since $(l_j)$ is an $R$-basis of $E$. Clear the finitely many denominators of these coefficients to obtain $0\ne t\in k[X]$ with $tV\subset A\cap E$. By step 3, $tV$ has an orthogonal $k$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ for $\sigma$. Since these vectors and all their $k$-linear combinations lie in $E$, step 1 identifies this with orthogonality for $s$. By [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm], $s(t^{-1}z)=|t|_R^{-1}s(z)$ for $z\in E$. Thus $v'_i=t^{-1}b_i$ is a $k$-basis of $V$ and $$s(\sum_i a_iv'_i)=|t|_R^{-1}\max_i |a_i|s(b_i)=\max_i|a_i|s(v'_i).$$ For $V=0$ choose the empty basis and use $s(0)=0$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.3/2, p.215: restriction to L; explicit common-denominator argument for a prescribed finite k-subspace.

from.place: Historical analytic input supporting the normalization chain from lem-trf-local-term-locality, through Temkin Theorem 3.5.5 Step 2: Distinguished presentations of reduced affinoids over an algebraically closed field. This is below the node level, not a replacement of the current contracting-correspondence unit proof. Supporting analytic lemma in the presentation construction: Norm-preserving lifts for a Tate epimorphism surjective on canonical reductions. Independent analytic input: Finite affinoid maps are finite on spectral unit balls over an algebraically closed field. Proof input: Orthogonal spectral norm on the fraction field of a finite affinoid domain. Supporting input: Stability of the Gauss fraction field of a Tate algebra. BGR stability proof input: Sections 5.3.3–5.3.4, especially Proposition 5.3.3/3 and the conclusion of Section 5.3.4, printed pp.215 and 218–220 (scan PDF pp.221 and 224–226); Section 5.3.4 removes the divisible-value-group restriction. Supporting input for the present split: Proposition 5.3.3/2, printed pp.214–215 (scan PDF pp.220–221).

split_report.summary: O2 read the BGR primary scan at pp.214-215 and 171-175. The coefficient-field statement is retained. Construct a finite reduced Tate model inside the spectral completion, use norm-attaining evaluations and stability of k, then clear polynomial denominators for the prescribed finite k-subspace. The latest blueprint proof of lem-trf-local-term-locality instead uses contracting correspondences; this descendant split changes neither that unit nor its chapter. Whole-blueprint searches for cartesian, orthogonal basis, spectral norm, maximum modulus, norming and spectral completion found no matching blueprint statement. Steps 1-2 realize the BGR completion diagram and finite Tate model; steps 3-4 expand its cartesianness and restriction argument.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-O2-8aa09915b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 3 new nodes and every cited statement, and checked the maths myself. BGR is not in literature/ (the worker recorded WANTED and the proof is marked by:agent), so I could not open BGR 5.3.3/2, 3.8.1/7 or 3.8.1/10. (1) scalar-envelope is true. C=H·E is finite and closed over H. N is power-multiplicative and definite, so M is reduced. N<=sigma follows from the monic relation. sigma_{M/Q}(e)=s(e) because the minimal polynomial over Q divides the one over R, and the spectral value is the largest root absolute value. It differs from weak-spectral-completion-product and power-multiplicative-algebra-norm-unique. (2) Tate norming-evaluations is true. A splits into minimal-prime components, sigma equals the sup over Max A (fibre-polynomial and supremum-calculus nodes exist for this), the maximum modulus principle gives attainment, and positivity follows from reducedness. n=0 checked. It is not a duplicate of supremum-calculus, minimal-component or fibre-polynomial. (3) The norming criterion holds over any valued field. A coordinate functional of the orthogonal basis of W_u, pulled back along f_u, splits off ku orthogonally, and induction on dim V finishes. The test norm |a+b xi| with xi in k-hat minus k is not cartesian and admits no norming maps, which is consistent. It differs from cartesian-subspace and cartesian-subspace-scalar-tower. Item steps 1-4 are correct: the isometric embedding of Q in R-hat; h_i^j c_ij in k[X], so A is finite, reduced and torsion-free with (T\0)^{-1}A=M; sigma|_A as a sup of contractive attaining seminorms, plus stability of k, then the criterion; and the denominator t in k[X] with tV inside A∩E and s(t^{-1}z)=|t|^{-1}s(z). No cycle (BFS). All citations are within unit sk-i-curve-zero, so no tool_uses. The item statement is unchanged, and the new nodes carry blueprint from/via, same_as=[] and 4 search kinds. No fixes.
